_about: AI debt: the named financings tracker and SemiAnalysis's forecast path. Read by AI Economy → Compute (the AI debt-market panel) and by the AI financing check on AI Economy → Tensions (server/tensions/checks/ai-financing.js). Amounts in $B. Add a row to `deals` whenever a headline AI financing lands; that is the whole upkeep. date = announcement month (some approximate). contingent: true marks money that is not owed yet: a guarantee (Nvidia's revenue backstop) or a standby facility that is only drawn on conditions, such as a supplier's commitment to buy notes or stock. Listed but left out of the cumulative total. Committed facilities count even while undrawn (a revolver, a delayed-draw loan, equipment leases signed but not yet paying rent), as they always have here. The Anthropic rows come from its S-1 (EDGAR, filed 2026-10-26); the Broadcom equipment leases are counted at rent excluding interest, and the $42B Broadcom note facility that can pay that rent is contingent so the same money is not counted twice.

forecast.note: AI debt becomes the second-largest US credit market after mortgages (~$13T): ~$7T outstanding by 2029 against ~$11.1T of cumulative AI capex 2024-29. Only the endpoints are theirs.
forecast.pathNote: Illustrative glide path to the $7T endpoint, for scale on the chart; only the end-2029 point is SemiAnalysis's.
